newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: CA sale good for Austrian taxpayers - FinMin Klima. [CORRECTED 12:07 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CA sale good for Austrian taxpayers - FinMin Klima. [CORRECTED 12:07 GMT]

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima said on Sunday the sale of flagship bank Creditanstalt to market leader Bank Austria was in the best interest of the country's taxpayers.
"The sale was successful, especially for the interests of the Austrian taxpayer and for the shareholders of Creditanstalt. We managed to get the best possible price," he told a news conference.
According to a brief statement handed out before the news conference, Bank Austria paid 17.161 billion schillings for control of its main rival, or 861 schillings per voting share.
Bank Austria outbid a rival group of industrial and financial interests led by insurer EA-Generali by almost three billion schillings, the statement said.
The deal was struck after an 11-hour emergency session of coalition leaders of the dominant Social Democrats and the conservative People's Party.

As part of the agreement, Bank Austria -- effectively controlled by the Social Democrat-led City of Vienna and part state-owned -- is to be taken out of public control progressively over the next seven (corrects from five) years, a key demand of the conservatives.
